# Bookkeeping HTTP API

HTTP API of the ALICE Bookkeeping. **Internal use only.**

> Work in progress: not every resource is documented yet. Only the sections listed below exist.

## Authentication
Every request carries a JWT in the `token` **query parameter** (e.g. `GET /api/tags?token=<jwt>`).
The token's `access` claim lists the user's roles; operations marked with a role below return `403` otherwise.

## Response envelope
Successful responses are `{ "data": ... }`, with `meta.page` added on paginated endpoints.
Failed responses are `{ "errors": [ { status, title, detail?, source? } ] }`.
Note that request-validation failures are sent with **HTTP 400** while each error's `status` field says `"422"`.

## Conventions
- Filters use bracket syntax: `filter[partialText]=foo`. List-valued filters are comma separated: `filter[ids]=1,2,3`.
- Pagination uses `page[limit]` and `page[offset]`.
- Timestamps are Unix epoch **milliseconds**.
- Operations flagged `x-llm-exclude: true` change data and are **not meant for LLMs or MCP tools**; skip them when generating tools.

## Instructions for LLMs and automated agents
- **Always paginate** when an endpoint supports `page[limit]` and `page[offset]`. Never rely on the default: when `page[limit]` is omitted the server
  may return up to 5000 items, which is far too much for a model context.
- **Request at most 100 items per call** (`page[limit]=100`). This is a rule for LLMs and agents, not a server limit (the server accepts more).
- To read more, repeat the call increasing `page[offset]` by the limit until `offset` reaches `meta.page.totalCount`.
- Prefer narrowing the request with `filter[...]` parameters over reading everything and filtering afterwards.
- Endpoints that are not paginated (for example `GET /tags`) return everything: use their filters.
- Do not call operations flagged `x-llm-exclude: true`: they create, change or delete data.

## Quick start

The examples below read the server address and the JWT from the environment:

```bash
export BOOKKEEPING_URL=http://localhost:4000
export TOKEN=<your jwt>
```

`curl -g` is needed because of the `[` `]` in filter names. Note that a token in the URL ends up in shell history and server logs.

## Tags

Labels attached to logs (and runs). Each tag may notify an e-mail list and a Mattermost channel.

### `GET /tags` - List tags

Operation id: `listTags`

Returns every tag matching the filters, **not paginated**.
Returns `204 No Content` (empty body) when nothing matches, so clients must not assume a JSON body.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filter[ids]` | query | string | no | Comma separated tag ids. |
| `filter[texts]` | query | string | no | Comma separated exact tag texts. Takes precedence over `filter[partialText]`. |
| `filter[partialText]` | query | string | no | Substring match on the tag text. Ignored when `filter[texts]` is given. |
| `filter[emails]` | query | string | no | Comma separated e-mail addresses. |
| `filter[mattermosts]` | query | string | no | Comma separated Mattermost channel names. |

Responses:

- `200`: Matching tags.
- `204`: No tag matches the filters. No body.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/tags?token=$TOKEN"
```

### `POST /tags` - Create a tag (not for LLM use)

Operation id: `createTag`

**Not meant for LLM or MCP tool use** (`x-llm-exclude`).

**Required role:** `admin`

Request body (JSON):

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | string | yes | Words, digits, `-` and `+` only. min length 2, max length 20, pattern `[\w\|\-+]{1,}` |
| `description` | string \| null | no | max length 100 |
| `mattermost` | string \| null | no |  |
| `email` | string \| null | no | One or more e-mail addresses, comma separated. |
| `color` | string \| null | no | pattern `^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$` |

Responses:

- `201`: The created tag.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.
- `403`: The token lacks the role required by this operation.
- `409`: A tag with the same text already exists.

```bash
curl -g -X POST "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/tags?token=$TOKEN" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"text":"FOOD","description":"Food related issues","email":"cake@cern.ch,test@cern.ch","mattermost":"food-channel","color":"#ff8800"}'
```

### `GET /tags/name` - Get a tag by its text

Operation id: `getTagByName`

Looks a tag up by its exact text (case as stored). Use this when you know the label but not the id.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | query | string | yes | Exact tag text. Must be URL-encoded. |

Responses:

- `200`: The tag.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.
- `404`: The requested entity does not exist.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/tags/name?name=FOOD&token=$TOKEN"
```

### `PUT /tags/{tagId}` - Update a tag (not for LLM use)

Operation id: `updateTag`

Only `description`, `email`, `mattermost`, `color` and `archivedAt` can change;
the tag `text` is immutable. Set `archivedAt` to a date to archive the tag and to `null` to restore it.

**Not meant for LLM or MCP tool use** (`x-llm-exclude`).

**Required role:** `admin`

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tagId` | path | integer | yes | Tag identifier. |

Request body (JSON):

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | string \| null | no | max length 100 |
| `mattermost` | string \| null | no |  |
| `email` | string \| null | no | One or more e-mail addresses, comma separated. |
| `color` | string \| null | no | pattern `^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$` |
| `archivedAt` | string \| integer \| null (date-time) | no | Date to archive the tag, either an ISO 8601 date-time string or epoch milliseconds, null to restore it. |

Responses:

- `201`: The updated tag. (Status is `201`, not `200`.)
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.
- `403`: The token lacks the role required by this operation.
- `404`: The requested entity does not exist.

```bash
curl -g -X PUT "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/tags/1?token=$TOKEN" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"description":"Updated description","archivedAt":null}'
```

## Shifts

Data used to fill end-of-shift reports.

### `GET /shift-data` - Get the data of the pending shift of the calling user

Operation id: `getShiftData`

Returns what a shifter needs to write their end-of-shift (EoS) report for the **pending shift**: the current shift, or the previous one
during the 30 minutes that follow its end. Shifts last 8 hours and are Night (23h-7h), Morning (7h-15h) and Afternoon (15h-23h) in the
Geneva time zone. The shift is deduced from the current time and the calling user, not from a parameter.

`typeSpecific` depends on `shiftType`: `{ environments }` for `ECS`, `{ runs }` for `QC/PDP`, `{ runs, tagsCounters }` for `SL`, and `null`
for `SLIMOS` and `DCS`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shiftType` | query | string | yes | Kind of shift. |

Responses:

- `200`: The shift data.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.
- `404`: The calling user is not known to Bookkeeping.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/shift-data?shiftType=ECS&token=$TOKEN"
```

## Simulation passes

Monte Carlo simulation productions.

### `GET /simulationPasses` - List simulation passes

Operation id: `listSimulationPasses`

Returns a page of simulation passes with their statistics (number of runs, data passes and logs).
Default order is by name, descending.

List filters are repeated query parameters: `filter[ids][]=1&filter[ids][]=2`. A single value without `[]` is rejected. Filters are combined
with AND.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filter[ids][]` | query | integer | no | Keep the simulation passes with one of these ids. Repeat the parameter for several values. |
| `filter[names][]` | query | string | no | Keep the simulation passes with one of these exact names. Repeat the parameter for several values. |
| `filter[lhcPeriodIds][]` | query | integer | no | Keep the simulation passes used by data passes of one of these LHC periods. Repeat the parameter for several values. |
| `filter[dataPassIds][]` | query | integer | no | Keep the simulation passes anchored to one of these data passes. Repeat the parameter for several values. |
| `sort[id]` | query | string | no | Sort by id. |
| `sort[name]` | query | string | no | Sort by name (the default is `desc`). |
| `sort[pwg]` | query | string | no | Sort by physics working group. |
| `sort[jiraId]` | query | string | no | Sort by Jira ticket. |
| `sort[requestedEventsCount]` | query | string | no | Sort by number of requested events. |
| `sort[generatedEventsCount]` | query | string | no | Sort by number of generated events. |
| `sort[outputSize]` | query | string | no | Sort by output size. |
| `page[limit]` | query | integer | no | Maximum number of items to return. LLMs and agents must use 100 or less. |
| `page[offset]` | query | integer | no | Number of items to skip. |

Responses:

- `200`: A page of simulation passes.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/simulationPasses?page[limit]=100&token=$TOKEN"
```

### `GET /simulationPasses/{id}` - Get a simulation pass by id

Operation id: `getSimulationPass`

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | integer | yes | Simulation pass identifier. |

Responses:

- `200`: The simulation pass.

## LHC periods statistics

LHC periods with statistics on their physics runs.

### `GET /lhcPeriodsStatistics` - List LHC periods with their statistics

Operation id: `listLhcPeriodsStatistics`

Returns a page of LHC periods with statistics computed on their **physics runs**: number of runs, average center-of-mass energy, distinct
energies, PDP beam types and number of data and simulation passes. Default order is by id, descending.

List filters are repeated query parameters: `filter[ids][]=1&filter[ids][]=2`. A single value without `[]` is rejected. Unknown query
parameters are rejected.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filter[ids][]` | query | integer | no | Keep the LHC periods with one of these ids. Repeat the parameter for several values. |
| `filter[names][]` | query | string | no | Keep the LHC periods with one of these exact names. Repeat the parameter for several values. |
| `filter[years][]` | query | integer | no | Keep the LHC periods of these years. The year is read from the period name (`LHC23f` is 2023). Repeat the parameter for several values. |
| `filter[pdpBeamTypes][]` | query | string | no | Keep the LHC periods having runs of one of these PDP beam types. Repeat the parameter for several values. |
| `sort[id]` | query | string | no | Sort by id (the default is `desc`). |
| `sort[name]` | query | string | no | Sort by name. |
| `sort[avgCenterOfMassEnergy]` | query | string | no | Sort by average center-of-mass energy. |
| `sort[year]` | query | string | no | Sort by year. |
| `sort[pdpBeamTypes]` | query | string | no | Sort by PDP beam types. |
| `page[limit]` | query | integer | no | Maximum number of items to return. LLMs and agents must use 100 or less. |
| `page[offset]` | query | integer | no | Number of items to skip. |

Responses:

- `200`: A page of LHC periods with statistics.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/lhcPeriodsStatistics?page[limit]=100&token=$TOKEN"
```

## GAQ detectors

Detectors whose QC flags contribute to the global aggregated quality (GAQ) of a run in a data pass.

### `GET /gaqDetectors` - List the detectors contributing to the GAQ of a run in a data pass

Operation id: `listGaqDetectors`

Returns the detectors whose QC flags contribute to the global aggregated quality (GAQ) of a run in a data pass, sorted by name. Not paginated.
The list is empty when no detector is set for this run and data pass, **or when the run or the data pass does not exist** (never `404`).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dataPassId` | query | integer | yes | Data pass identifier. |
| `runNumber` | query | integer | yes | Run number. |

Responses:

- `200`: The detectors.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/gaqDetectors?dataPassId=3&runNumber=56&token=$TOKEN"
```

### `POST /gaqDetectors` - Set the detectors contributing to the GAQ of runs in a data pass (not for LLM use)

Operation id: `setGaqDetectors`

Requires the role `admin` or `gaq`. For each given run, replaces the detectors contributing to the GAQ in the data pass by the given ones.
Every run must be linked to the data pass and have every given detector.

**Not meant for LLM or MCP tool use** (`x-llm-exclude`).

**Required role:** `admin`, `gaq`

Request body (JSON):

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dataPassId` | integer | yes |  |
| `runNumbers` | array | yes | Run numbers of the runs to update, without duplicates. |
| `detectorIds` | array | yes | Ids of the detectors contributing to the GAQ, without duplicates. |

Responses:

- `201`: The created associations between runs and detectors, one per run and detector.
- `400`: The request failed validation (see the validation errors format), **or** a run is not linked to the data pass, a detector does not exist or a run does not have a given detector. In these last cases the error has `title: Service unavailable` and the reason in `detail`.
- `403`: The token lacks the role required by this operation.
- `404`: The data pass does not exist.

```bash
curl -g -X POST "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/gaqDetectors?token=$TOKEN" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"dataPassId":3,"runNumbers":[49,56],"detectorIds":[4,7]}'
```

## End of shift reports

End-of-shift (EoS) reports written by the shifters.

### `POST /eos-report` - Create the end-of-shift report of the calling user (not for LLM use)

Operation id: `createEosReport`

Creates the end-of-shift (EoS) report of the **pending shift** of the calling user (see `GET /shift-data`) as a log entry. The start of the shift is
deduced from the current time and must **not** be given in the body.

The text of the report is generated from the body and from the data of the shift (issues, environments, runs...), the log is linked to the runs and to
the environments of the shift and is tagged with the tags of the shift type that exist.

**Not meant for LLM or MCP tool use** (`x-llm-exclude`).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reportType` | query | string | yes | Kind of shift the report is about. |

Request body (JSON):

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shifterName` | string | no | Name of the shifter. |
| `traineeName` | string | no |  |
| `lhcTransitions` | string | no | Transitions of the LHC machine during the shift. |
| `shiftFlow` | string | no |  |
| `infoForNextShifter` | string | no |  |
| `infoForRmRc` | string | no | Information for the run coordinator and the resource manager. |
| `runs` | array | no | Accepted but not used. |
| `typeSpecific` | object \| null | yes | Depends on `reportType`, and must be given (`null` for `SLIMOS`): - `ECS`: `{ environmentComments, runComments }`, objects mapping an environment id or a run number to a comment - `QC/PDP`: `{ runComments }` - `SL`: `{ magnets }` - `DCS`: `{ alerts }`  |

Responses:

- `201`: The log entry created for the report.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.
- `404`: The calling user is not known to Bookkeeping.

```bash
curl -g -X POST "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/eos-report?reportType=ECS&token=$TOKEN" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"shifterName":"John Doe","shiftFlow":"The shift flow","infoForNextShifter":"Info for the next shifter","typeSpecific":{"environmentComments":{"ENV1":"A comment about the environment"},"runComments":{"200":"A comment about the run"}}}'
```

## Attachments

Files attached to log entries.

### `POST /attachments` - Upload a file as an attachment (not for LLM use)

Operation id: `createAttachment`

Uploads **one** file (multipart request) and stores it as an attachment, linked to a log if `log` is given.

The files of a request are all written on the server, but only the first one is stored as an attachment. A request without any file is rejected with a `400`.
Logs and their attachments are usually created together with `POST /logs`.

**Not meant for LLM or MCP tool use** (`x-llm-exclude`).

Request body (multipart/form-data):

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `log` | integer | no | Identifier of the log to attach the file to. |
| `attachments` | string (binary) | yes | The file to upload. |

Responses:

- `201`: The stored attachment.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.

```bash
curl -g -X POST "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/attachments?token=$TOKEN" \
  -F 'log=1' \
  -F 'attachments=@/path/to/file.png'
```

### `GET /attachments/{attachmentId}` - Download the file of an attachment

Operation id: `getAttachmentFile`

Returns the content of the file, with the type of the file as `Content-Type`. Use `curl -OJ` to save it with the name given by the server.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `attachmentId` | path | integer | yes | Attachment identifier. |

Responses:

- `200`: The file.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.
- `404`: No attachment has this id.

```bash
curl -g -OJ "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/attachments/1?token=$TOKEN"
```

## DPL processes

Processes of the data processing layer (DPL) executed during the runs, by detector, process and host.

### `GET /dpl-process/detectors` - List the detectors having an executed process in a run

Operation id: `listDplDetectorsWithExecutedProcesses`

Returns the detectors that have at least one executed DPL process in the run, sorted by name. Not paginated. This is the first level of the
run details tree of DPL processes: detector, then process (`/dpl-process/processes`), then host (`/dpl-process/hosts`), then executions
(`/dpl-process/executions`).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `runNumber` | query | integer | yes | Run number. |

Responses:

- `200`: The detectors.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.
- `404`: The run, the detector, the process or the host does not exist.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/dpl-process/detectors?runNumber=106&token=$TOKEN"
```

### `GET /dpl-process/processes` - List the processes executed for a detector in a run

Operation id: `listDplProcessesExecutedForDetector`

Returns the DPL processes that have been executed at least once in the run for the detector, sorted by name, with their type. Not paginated.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `runNumber` | query | integer | yes | Run number. |
| `detectorId` | query | integer | yes | Identifier of the detector (the detectors of `GET /detectors`). |

Responses:

- `200`: The processes.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.
- `404`: The run, the detector, the process or the host does not exist.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/dpl-process/processes?runNumber=106&detectorId=1&token=$TOKEN"
```

### `GET /dpl-process/hosts` - List the hosts on which a process was executed for a detector in a run

Operation id: `listHostsExecutingDplProcess`

Returns the hosts on which the DPL process has been executed at least once in the run for the detector, sorted by host name. Not paginated.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `runNumber` | query | integer | yes | Run number. |
| `detectorId` | query | integer | yes | Identifier of the detector (the detectors of `GET /detectors`). |
| `processId` | query | integer | yes | Identifier of the DPL process. |

Responses:

- `200`: The hosts.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.
- `404`: The run, the detector, the process or the host does not exist.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/dpl-process/hosts?runNumber=106&detectorId=1&processId=1&token=$TOKEN"
```

### `GET /dpl-process/executions` - List the executions of a process on a host for a detector in a run

Operation id: `listDplProcessExecutions`

Returns the executions of the DPL process on the host in the run for the detector. Not paginated.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `runNumber` | query | integer | yes | Run number. |
| `detectorId` | query | integer | yes | Identifier of the detector (the detectors of `GET /detectors`). |
| `processId` | query | integer | yes | Identifier of the DPL process. |
| `hostId` | query | integer | yes | Host identifier. |

Responses:

- `200`: The executions.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.
- `404`: The run, the detector, the process or the host does not exist.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/dpl-process/executions?runNumber=106&detectorId=1&processId=1&hostId=1&token=$TOKEN"
```

## FLPs

Roles of FLPs in runs, with their data counters.

### `GET /flps` - List the FLP roles

Operation id: `listFlps`

Returns the roles of FLPs (one entry per FLP and per run) with their data counters. Paginated, sorted by name descending by default.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page[limit]` | query | integer | no | Maximum number of items to return. LLMs and agents must use 100 or less. |
| `page[offset]` | query | integer | no | Number of items to skip. |
| `sort[id]` | query | string | no | Sort by identifier. |
| `sort[name]` | query | string | no | Sort by FLP name. |
| `sort[hostname]` | query | string | no | Sort by host name. |
| `sort[runNumber]` | query | string | no | Sort by run number. |

Responses:

- `200`: A page of FLP roles.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/flps?page[limit]=100&token=$TOKEN"
```

### `POST /flps` - Create an FLP role (not for LLM use)

Operation id: `createFlp`

Creates the role of an FLP in a run.

**Not meant for LLM or MCP tool use** (`x-llm-exclude`).

Request body (JSON):

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes | min length 1 |
| `hostname` | string | yes | min length 1 |
| `runNumber` | integer | yes |  |
| `nTimeframes` | number | no |  |
| `bytesProcessed` | number | no |  |
| `bytesEquipmentReadOut` | number | no |  |
| `bytesRecordingReadOut` | number | no |  |
| `bytesFairMQReadOut` | number | no |  |
| `subtype` | string | no |  |

Responses:

- `201`: The created FLP role.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.

```bash
curl -g -X POST "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/flps?token=$TOKEN" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"FLP-1","hostname":"flp001.cern.ch","runNumber":106}'
```

### `GET /flps/{flpId}` - Get an FLP role

Operation id: `getFlp`

Returns one FLP role, with its run.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `flpId` | path | integer | yes | FLP role identifier. |

Responses:

- `200`: The FLP role.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.
- `404`: The requested entity does not exist.

```bash
curl -g "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/flps/1?token=$TOKEN"
```

### `PATCH /flps/{flpName}/runs/{runNumber}` - Update the counters of an FLP in a run (not for LLM use)

Operation id: `updateFlp`

Replaces the data counters of the FLP role identified by FLP name and run number. Counters absent from the body are set to null.
Responds 400 if the run or the FLP in this run does not exist.

**Not meant for LLM or MCP tool use** (`x-llm-exclude`).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `flpName` | path | string | yes | Name of the FLP. |
| `runNumber` | path | integer | yes | Run number. |

Request body (JSON):

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `nTimeframes` | integer | no |  |
| `bytesProcessed` | integer | no |  |
| `bytesEquipmentReadOut` | integer | no |  |
| `bytesRecordingReadOut` | integer | no |  |
| `bytesFairMQReadOut` | integer | no |  |

Responses:

- `201`: The updated FLP role.
- `400`: The request failed validation. HTTP status is 400 although each error's `status` field is `"422"`. `source.pointer` has the form `/data/attributes/<query|params|body>/<field>`.

```bash
curl -g -X PATCH "$BOOKKEEPING_URL/api/flps/1/runs/1?token=$TOKEN" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"nTimeframes":1000,"bytesProcessed":2048}'
```
